text:
AROUND TOWN
Scots Day
TICONDEROGA, N.Y. — Fort Ticonderoga invites visitors to celebrate Scottish heritage from 9:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Saturday, June 13.
Explore Scottish clan tents and vendors, featuring kilts, crafts and Celtic goods; witness musket demonstrations showcasing Highland soldiers and their weapons; march alongside clans and the Black Watch to a memorial ceremony at the Scottish Cairn; experience the sounds of fifes, drums, bagpipes and traditional Scottish music performances, discover the evolution of Highland military uniforms, uncover Scottish stories hidden within Ticonderoga’s collections, and take part in the ceremonial Presentation of the Haggis celebrating Scottish tradition and community.
Admission: $30/adult, $28/senior; $14/child; free for Fort Ticonderoga members, Ambassador Pass holders, and children age 4 and under.
Book sale
RUTLAND — The June Friends of Rutland Free Library Book Sale will be held from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Friday and Saturday, June 12 and 13, at 10 Court St. in Rutland. Featured are thousands of organized, gently used books, CDs, DVDs and puzzles for all ages, as well as a selection of rare and antique books. All purchases by donation only. Limit of two grocery bags per monthly sale per family. No book dealers. Proceeds support library programs, collections and designated projects.
Writers for Recovery
RUTLAND — Free and open to the public, a celebration of Writers for Recovery will be held from 6:30 to 8 p.m. Friday, June 12, at The Hub Streetside Conference Center, 67 Merchants Row Suite 201, Rutland.
Listen to stories, poems and songs about living and recovering from addiction of all kinds. There will be live music by Nick Patyk and refreshments to accompany the poetic performances, featuring Kelly Kelsey, Gregory Higgins, Ellen McLoughlin, Jaci Penelope, Aiden Alexander, plus more voices.
Smithsonian exhibit
Vermont Humanities is partnering with New Hampshire Humanities and the Smithsonian’s Museum on Main Street program to bring a traveling exhibit, Spark! Places of Innovation, to small towns in Vermont and New Hampshire. The exhibit explores the combination of places, people and circumstances that spark innovation and invention in rural communities.
Each state will support three host sites, and each location will host the exhibit for six weeks. In Vermont,
June-July — Rockingham Free Public Library in Bellows Falls.
July-August — Barnet Public Library.
September-October — Swanton Public Library.
For more information, visit www.vermonthumanities.org/programs/attend/museum-on-main-street/spark.
AROUND VT
From UVM Extension
Vermonters are urged to take steps to protect the state’s forests and outdoor spaces during PlayCleanGo Awareness Week, June 6-13. Led by North American Invasive Species Management Association, this national, annual campaign encourages outdoor recreationists to help stop the spread of introduced species harmful to local ecosystems.
The message is Play – Enjoy Vermont outdoors responsibly; Clean – Brush off mud, seeds and debris from gear, boots and pets; Go – Head out to your next destination with clean equipment.
From DEC
The Vermont Lakes and Ponds Program’s Shoreland Best Management Practices offer guidance to help property owners protect and restore their lakeside properties to benefit lake health and shoreline habitat.
The Shoreland Protection Act regulates new activities in protected shoreland areas that are within 250 feet of the shoreline of lakes and ponds that have a surface area of 10 or more acres. Property owners need a Shoreland Protection Permit for activities in protected shoreland areas that create cleared areas (removing vegetation like trees or shrubs or disturbing the natural ground cover) or impervious surfaces (any hard or solid surfaces like roofs, roads, and parking lots where water runs off instead of soaking into the ground).
Shoreland property owners can use the Sharing the Edge booklet to learn more.
For owners who want to go above and beyond shoreland regulations, the Lake Wise Program offers free technical assistance to support lake-friendly living.
For any Lake Wise questions, call 802-490-6128 or email Alison.Marchione@Vermont.gov.
